title: Education Station Page Foundry
description: A bounded queue that builds one coherent page at a time and extracts reusable Studio systems before moving on.

stopConditions: Build or strict type check fails
Required API has no honest fallback
The design repeats a recent page without educational reason
A destructive repository-wide migration is required

items.title: Animal Diversity & Taxonomy
items.organizingPrinciple: Nested evolutionary lineage, taxonomic rank, and divergence in animal body plans.
items.learnerQuestion: How can one branching history produce the enormous variety of animal forms?
contentScope: Major animal lineages and body plans
Species concepts and the limits of rank

dataSource.label: Curated phylogeny with live taxon records

visual.topology: Luminous branching phylogenetic canopy with rank-aware zoom
visual.evocation: A living cabinet of life growing outward from deep shared ancestry.
visual.backgroundMeaning: Roots are older ancestry; forks are divergence; leaf clusters are living lineages.
visual.backgroundMotion: Slow pulses travel from trunk to tips while selected clades illuminate.
avoid: Reuse of the Zoology atlas modal rhythm
visual.interaction: Move through ranks, open a clade, pin two lineages, and compare inherited body-plan features.

studioContributions.label: Branching tree topology
studioContributions.description: A reusable hierarchy for ancestry, dependencies, and branching concepts.

studioContributions.label: Taxonomic path
studioContributions.description: A rank-aware path that can compare parallel branches.

studioContributions.label: Phylogenetic canopy
studioContributions.description: A vivid background whose branches communicate ancestry and divergence.

items.notes: Teach lineage rather than reproducing the collection atlas.

items.title: Comparative Zoology
items.organizingPrinciple: Compare how different body plans solve the same functional problem.
items.learnerQuestion: How can different structures perform similar jobs—and similar structures perform different jobs?

dataSource.label: Curated trait matrix with live animal profiles
dataSource.provider: Local trait matrix plus iNaturalist taxa

visual.topology: Synchronized comparison chamber with aligned anatomical layers
visual.evocation: A comparative anatomy laboratory where function appears before terminology.
visual.backgroundMeaning: Layered silhouettes expose shared constraints while active systems glow.
visual.backgroundMotion: Matched actions play in parallel and functional systems pulse together.
avoid: Branching tree from the previous page
visual.interaction: Choose a function and specimens, align structures, scrub matched motion, and reveal tradeoffs.

studioContributions.label: Synchronized comparison
studioContributions.description: Parallel specimens sharing one control timeline and semantic row system.

studioContributions.label: Trait matrix
studioContributions.description: A compact comparison matrix linked to visual specimens.

studioContributions.label: Anatomical layer field
studioContributions.description: A subject-aware field of translucent silhouettes and active systems.

items.notes: Make function visible before naming every structure.

items.title: Ethology
items.organizingPrinciple: Behavior unfolds as signals, decisions, feedback, learning, and social interaction.
items.learnerQuestion: How does an animal turn information into action?

dataSource.label: Curated behavior sequences with optional media and taxon records

visual.topology: Behavior timeline connected to a signal network and editable ethogram
visual.evocation: A moonlit field station where tracks, calls, gaze, and social signals become traces.
visual.backgroundMood: Nocturnal, alert, rhythmic, social, full of faint traces
visual.backgroundMeaning: Paths, waves, and links represent observable behavior and communication.
visual.backgroundMotion: Signals propagate between animals while the timeline records changing states.
visual.interaction: Choose a scenario, scrub a sequence, code events in an ethogram, and compare individual and group outcomes.

studioContributions.label: Behavior sequence
studioContributions.description: A causal timeline for stimulus, state, action, consequence, and feedback.

studioContributions.label: Ethogram
studioContributions.description: An observation table and timeline for coding events and duration.

studioContributions.label: Field trace environment
studioContributions.description: A vivid layer of tracks, calls, motion trails, and social signals.

items.notes: Learners should classify behavior from evidence, not only read definitions.
